title: BofA Sees Chip Market Nearly Doubling to $3.2 Trillion by 2030, Names ETFs
excerpt: BofA’s Vivek Arya projects the semiconductor market nearly doubling by 2030, with memory leading and equipment spend more than doubling — naming Nvidia, AMD, Marvell and two chip-gear stocks plus five ETFs.
body:
• Bank of America’s semiconductor analysts, led by Vivek Arya, forecast the global semiconductor market nearly doubling to $3.2 trillion by 2030 from $1.7 trillion in 2026, in a September 14, 2026 report.
  • Memory is the biggest growth engine: $937 billion to $1.8 trillion; core semiconductors $739 billion to $1.35 trillion; server-related sales $359 billion to $848 billion; wafer-fab equipment spending more than doubles to $359.8 billion.
  • The rationale: 2027 is “largely fully booked and contracted” across compute, networking and memory; supply stays tight into 2028. The biggest risk is a hyperscaler AI-spending slowdown.
  • BofA’s preferred names (all Buy): Nvidia ($350 target), AMD ($620), Marvell ($365), Lam Research ($385), Applied Materials ($650) — plus ETFs SMH, SOXX, SOXQ (Strong Buy) and XSD, PSI (Buy).

Wall Street is putting its weight behind the AI infrastructure buildout — with numbers that dwarf the recent sell-off. Bank of America’s semiconductor team, led by Vivek Arya, projects the global semiconductor market will nearly double to $3.2 trillion by 2030 from $1.7 trillion in 2026, according to a September 14, 2026 report covered by Zacks and TheStreet. The message: contracted demand, not sentiment, should price the chip cycle.

The call lands as a deliberate counterweight to the mid-September AI sell-off. The PHLX Semiconductor Index has gained about 91% over the past year and roughly 59% year-to-date — but it stumbled on September 15 as AI-safety concerns flared, with Dario Amodei, Sam Altman and Elon Musk all calling for a more measured pace of frontier-model development. BofA’s forecast argues the buildout continues regardless: even under a more measured approach, the report’s reasoning runs, AI investment stays substantial because the orders are already booked.

“2027 remains largely fully booked and contracted across compute, networking and memory vendors.”

— Bank of America semiconductor analysts (via Zacks)

Where the growth comes from

Memory is the centerpiece: BofA sees the memory market growing from $937 billion in 2026 to $1.8 trillion by 2030, the largest absolute expansion in the industry. Core semiconductors rise from $739 billion to $1.35 trillion; server-related sales from $359 billion to $848 billion. And wafer-fabrication equipment spending more than doubles, from $155.9 billion to $359.8 billion — the picks-and-shovels corollary that validates the equipment bulls.

The underpinning is visibility. BofA reports no deterioration in customer orders, long-term agreements, capacity commitments or pricing, with 2027 “largely fully booked and contracted” across compute, networking and memory. Supply stays tight into 2028 on CPUs, XPU attach, optics-based scale-up solutions and AI accelerators from multiple ASIC and GPU vendors.

What BofA likes — and the caveat

The firm’s preferred names, all Buy-rated: Nvidia ($350 price target), AMD ($620) and Marvell ($365) in compute and networking; Analog Devices and onsemi in analog; and Lam Research ($385) and Applied Materials ($650) in equipment — the same equipment pair JPMorgan favors.

For investors who want the theme rather than the stocks, Zacks recommends five semiconductor ETFs: SMH (VanEck, $66.43 billion in assets, 0.35% fee, 26 holdings) and SOXX (iShares, $41.99 billion, 0.33% fee, 30 holdings), both ranked Strong Buy; SOXQ (Invesco PHLX, $2.87 billion, 0.19% fee) also Strong Buy; and XSD (State Street SPDR, $2.56 billion) and PSI (Invesco, $2.46 billion), both Buy.

The honest caveat is crowdedness. BofA’s own June 2026 fund manager survey found a record 80% of 198 managers — overseeing $540 billion — calling long-semiconductors the most crowded trade. The “fear of heights” sentiment coexists with the bullish forecast; the named risk is a hyperscaler AI-spending slowdown. BofA’s answer: the contracts are signed, and contracted demand outlasts sentiment.

nri_angle: For US-based Indian investors, BofA’s call frames the actionable AI-infrastructure trade: booked capacity through 2027, equipment spend doubling, and a named set of stocks and ETFs.
